metadata.title: Study Pods
metadata.description: Quiet, class-based study pods where classmates can see each other's progress.
metadata.landingTitle: Study Pods | Small study groups, scoped to your class
metadata.landingDescription: Study Pods puts 2–6 students from the same class into a pod, so you can see how far along everyone is on assignments and reports.

steps.heading: Three steps to get started
steps.step1Body: Join with the link, QR code or class code from your teacher or classmates. If your class isn’t there yet, you can create it.
steps.step2Body: Start a pod of 2–6 classmates, or accept an invitation to one.
steps.step3Title: Set a target and keep going
steps.step3Body: Set a goal, like a character count for a report or hours of study, and your progress is shared with your pod.

features.heading: How far you’ve got. Never what you wrote.
features.body: The text of your reports and drafts stays private, even from your pod.
features.barBody: How much of your report is written, or how many hours you’ve studied, at a glance. The report itself is never shared.
features.recentBody: When a podmate hasn’t logged in a while, their stamp changes color. It’s a cue to check in, not a mark against them.
features.nudgeBody: Send a short message to a podmate who seems stuck. There’s a daily limit, so nobody gets flooded.
features.docsBody: Count the characters in a Google Doc you choose, automatically. Study Pods opens only the file you pick, and never stores its text.

data.heading: What’s shared, and what isn’t
data.shared2: Your targets and how far along they are
data.private1: The text of your reports and assignments
data.private2: Your progress, to anyone outside your pod (even in the same class)
data.private3: What’s inside a connected Google Doc. Only the character count is recorded.

classLink.heading: One link, and the whole class lands in the same place.
classLink.body: When you create a class, you get a join link and a QR code. Put them on a lecture slide or a notice board, or fill the screen with Show in class, and students join the right class without searching.
classLink.qrNote: Ready to drop into a slide or a notice
classLink.figureLabel: Example: the join link study-pods.org/join/K7M3Q9TX for Statistics 201, the code K7M3 Q9TX, a QR code and a Show in class button

faq.heading: Before you start
faq.teacherQ: Can my professor see my progress?
faq.teacherA: No. Your progress is visible only to the members of your pod.
faq.passwordA: No. You log in with a 6-digit code (or the button) sent to your university email.
faq.podSizeQ: How many people can be in a pod?
faq.podSizeA: Up to six. Small groups make it easier to notice how everyone is doing.
faq.docsQ: What if I don’t use Google Docs?
faq.docsA: That’s fine. You can log characters written or hours studied yourself.
faq.anyClassQ: Does it work for any class?
faq.anyClassA: Yes. With an @andrew.ac.jp address, you can create or join a class for any course.

closing.heading: Start your next assignment in a pod.
closing.body: No password needed. We’ll send a login code to your @andrew.ac.jp address.
closing.cta: Log in with your university email

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Study Pods (“the service”) is a study app built and run by a student. This page explains what the service collects, how it’s used, and who can see it.
privacy.accountText: your university email address (@andrew.ac.jp) and display name
privacy.membershipText: the classes and pods you join
privacy.contentText: targets, progress logs, comments and nudges
privacy.googleLabel: If you connect Google Docs (a planned feature):
privacy.googleText: the character count and last-modified time of the documents you choose, and the Google access token needed to keep the connection working
privacy.cookieText: only to keep you logged in, remember your language, and remember two small display settings (whether you’ve chosen a display name, and whether you’ve seen the setup-complete message). No advertising or analytics cookies.
privacy.noText: We never store the text of your reports or assignments.
privacy.useText: Only to run the service (sharing progress with your pod, nudges and similar features) and for the research use in section 6. We don’t use your data for advertising, and we don’t sell it.
privacy.googleIntro: Connecting Google Docs isn’t available yet. Once it is, Google user data will be handled as follows.
privacy.google1: Connecting Google Docs is optional. If you do, the service can open only the documents you select in Google’s file picker (the drive.file permission). It cannot read the rest of your Google Drive.
privacy.google2: A document’s text is read only to count its characters, and is never stored, logged or shared. Only the count and last-modified time are saved.
privacy.google3: Access tokens are handled on our server only and are never shown to other users.
privacy.google4: You can disconnect Google at any time. We then delete the stored token.
privacy.limitedUse: Study Pods’ use and transfer of information received from Google APIs to any other app will adhere to the <link>Google API Services User Data Policy</link>, including the Limited Use requirements.
privacy.podText: your display name, your targets and progress, when you last logged, and your comments and nudges
privacy.classText: your display name, so they can invite you to a pod. Not your progress.
privacy.devText: can access the database to run the service and fix problems.
privacy.serviceGoogle: Google: only if you connect Google Docs
privacy.servicesNote: Supabase, Vercel and Resend are US companies. The database is stored in their Tokyo region.
privacy.researchText: Study Pods is part of a university capstone project. The project report uses only aggregated usage figures that can’t identify you, such as how often progress is logged or how many people keep using the app. It never includes names, email addresses, or the text of memos or comments. If you don’t want your data included, email us at the address below and we’ll leave it out of the analysis; you can keep using the app. Whether you use Study Pods, and whether you opt out, has no effect on your grades.
privacy.retentionText: We keep your data while you use your account. To delete your account and its data, email us at the address below; we’ll delete it within 30 days, including backups. Accounts with no login for one year are deleted. If the service shuts down, all data is deleted within 30 days. Logs kept by our hosting providers follow their own retention periods.
privacy.changesText: If this policy changes, we’ll update the effective date on this page.
privacy.priceText: Study Pods is currently free. If paid features are ever introduced, we’ll tell you in advance.
privacy.organizerLabel: Whoever created the class (e.g. a teacher):
privacy.organizerText: the number of members and the join link. Not your progress or targets.
